Let's also keep in mind that these warnings are exclusive to GDScript, therefore there's no need to be vague about it. In a script written in GDScript, the concept of "private" can be denoted with the `_` prefix, as this PR entails.
Something like...?


body:
Same thoughts as above.
```suggestion
			When set to [code]warn[/code] or [code]error[/code], produces a warning or an error respectively when a script's private method is called from an external script that does not inherit the original script. A method is considered private when its name begins with an underscore ([code]_[/code]).
```

It would be nice, but it's not exactly mandatory, to specify what it is instead of "member", similar to what's done in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104955 .

No need to change anything in this PR, it's for future reference

I'm not sure what _exactly_ to say here, but this warning is not always accurate. It's not that it "would cause problems". Rather, it's not intended and it _may_ cause problems.
Also we generally refer to "runtime" as when the _project_ is run, but this warning may also be sent for `tool` script meant to run in the editor.
```suggestion
			return vformat(R"(The member "%s" is private. It is not meant to be accessed from an external script.)", symbols[0]);
```
or
```suggestion
			return vformat(R"(The member "%s" is private. It should not be accessed from an external script.)", symbols[0]);
```
or, the opposite:
```suggestion
			return vformat(R"(The member "%s" is private. It should only be accessed by a script that inherits this member.)", symbols[0]);
```
Or similar? Or not at all? I'd like others to chime in as well.
Sentiment similar to prior review.
These changes really don't look valid, I don't see how removing the meta here is related to this PR?

> Why do we have to separate warnings and this one still says it's about methods as well?

~~It says *access*, not *call*. Also I should've spelled it as "method name" instead of this. XP~~
NVM I deleted the things in the brackets and the brackets themselves..

> `p_call->get_datatype()` what has the return type of the function to do with this?

That's used to check whether the access is triggered from self or an external class, and in this case, only `p_call` contains the real information about the accessor itself in its datatype.
When a reduce happens, it will try to figure out whether its `foo()` or `a.foo()`. Without this, everything will be invalid private access, even from implicit `self`.

This is definitely not doing what you think it is. The `datatype` of a `CallNode` contains the return type. But since you are accessing this in `reduce_call` it is not even set correctly yet. (as in it is always unresolved)

Why do you need the check in those cases anyway? If you can access the method by identifier or through `super` it has to be either some global, or it has to be from a class in the inheritance chain.
